### Observed differences

- In the later window, activities A27, A36, A37, A42 and A43 each appear in about half of traces (participation roughly 50–52%) instead of essentially all traces, and their mean occurrences per trace drop from about 1.0 to about 0.5. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
- A25’s outgoing routing changes sharply: before, it led to A42, A36, A43 and A37 with shares around 20–27% each; after, it leads to A28 in about 97–98% of its occurrences. [DIR001]
- A26’s routing also changes: before, about 99% of its outgoing transitions went to A27; after, about 48% go to A27 and the remainder is split among A37, A43, A42 and A36. [DIR002]
- A27 still leads to A31 in about 97% of its occurrences, but A27 itself is present in only about half of traces in the later window. [DIR003, OCC001]
- Positions shift: A36, A37, A42 and A43 move later (mean position from about 0.40 to about 0.58), while A28 moves earlier (from about 0.47 to 0.39), A26 earlier (from about 0.61 to 0.53), and A27 earlier (from about 0.64 to 0.58). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]
- A25 was before A36, A37, A42 and A43 in about 97–98% of traces before; after, this holds in about 49% of traces, with A25 occurring alone in about 49%. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005]
- A27 and the group A36/A37/A42/A43 almost never co-occur after the change (co-occurrence about 1–2%), whereas they co-occurred in all traces before. [REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016]
- The order between A28 and A36/A37/A42/A43 reverses: before, those activities preceded A28 in about 97–98% of traces; after, A28 precedes them in about 49% of traces and occurs without them in about 49%. [REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020]
- For A25 and A28, the lag changes from five steps apart in all observed pairs before to immediately adjacent (lag 1) in about 98% of pairs after. [LAG001]
- For A26 and A31, the dominant lag changes from 2 steps in about 97% of pairs before to a split between 2 steps (about 50%) and 5 steps (about 48%) after. [LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process now has two main branches: in about half of cases the earlier pattern continues, with A25 preceding A36/A37/A42/A43 and A26 preceding A27 before A31; in the other half, A27, A36, A37, A42 and A43 are skipped, A25 is followed almost immediately by A28, and A26 routes to A36/A37/A42/A43 or A27 depending on the branch. The number of qualifying evidence items (63) is far above the 0.83 expected by chance, and occurrence, routing, position, relation and lag indicators agree on the same underlying shift. A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the two windows reflect different case types or process variants rather than a modification of one process; also, some lag estimates for pairs involving A36/A37/A42/A43 in the later window rest on only one or two traces, so the exact lag structure of the new branch is uncertain. [OCC001, DIR001, DIR002, REL001, REL013, REL017, LAG001, LAG006]
